tweet_summary: A breaking-news account claims as confirmed fact that Iran's new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in a coma and had his leg amputated.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted: the tweet presents unverified rumors ('#BREAKING confirmed') about a head of state's medical condition as established fact, to 7.8M+ impressions. The coma/amputation claim traces to anonymous-sourced tabloid reporting (The Sun); it is NOT confirmed. That said, the situation is genuinely murky — Mojtaba did not appear publicly, a cardboard cutout was used at the succession rally, and state media labeled him 'janbaz' (disabled war veteran). International reporting indicated a fractured foot and minor facial injuries, and a statement was issued in his name via state TV (read by a presenter). So the correct note should flag the coma/amputation as unverified rather than assert a competing certainty.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note states that the coma-and-amputation claim is UNVERIFIED / not confirmed (traceable to anonymous tabloid sources), and ideally notes that Iran acknowledged he was injured and issued a statement in his name via state media. The note must NOT itself over-claim the opposite as settled fact — e.g. flatly asserting 'reliable sources report only minor injuries' as if his condition were clearly known is itself questionable given he made no public appearance and a cardboard cutout was used; the original note's overconfidence here is what drew opinion/speculation + incorrect ratings. A correct note acknowledges uncertainty on both sides: the specific coma/amputation claim is unconfirmed, while officials say he is injured but alive. FAIL if it endorses the coma/amputation as confirmed, or if it has no source.
reference_note: This is not confirmed. The coma-and-leg-amputation claim comes from anonymous-sourced tabloid reports and has not been verified. Iran acknowledged Mojtaba Khamenei was injured in the strike that killed his father and issued a statement in his name via state media; his exact condition remains unclear amid an information blackout. https://www.euronews.com/2026/03/12/missing-in-action-what-we-know-about-mojtaba-khameneis-condition

original_unhelpful_note.text: The claim that Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is confirmed to be in a coma and had his leg amputated is inaccurate. These are unverified rumors; reliable sources report only minor injuries, and he issued a statement via state media.    https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-new-supreme-leader-lightly-injured-still-active-iranian-official-tells-2026-03-11  https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/11/middleeast/mojtaba-khamenei-injuries-iran-supreme-leader-latam-intl
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Rated notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation (23) + notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded (21) + sources/incorrect. The note correctly calls the claim unverified, but then over-asserts the opposite ('reliable sources report only minor injuries') as settled — contestable given he made no public appearance and a cardboard cutout was used at the succession rally. Leaning on a single Iranian-official-sourced framing ('lightly injured, still active') without acknowledging the genuine uncertainty made the note read as taking a side.

fact_check.notes: Mojtaba Khamenei was injured in the strike that killed his father. Coma + amputation claims come from The Sun's anonymous sources and are not confirmed; international media reported a fractured foot and minor facial injuries. He made no public appearance (a cardboard cutout was used at the succession rally) and state media labeled him 'janbaz'/disabled war vet, so his true condition is genuinely uncertain. A statement was issued in his name, read by a TV presenter. Bottom line: the tweet's 'confirmed coma + amputation' is unverified; the opposite is also not cleanly established.

importance.lens_rationale: Wartime claims about the medical status of a nuclear-armed adversary's head of state can shape escalation dynamics; reducing unverified rumor here has real geopolitical value.
